title: Bangsar Hill Park: eight units a floor, with views to KL's towers.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #415 | BANGSAR HILL PARK, BANGSAR
excerpt: Two newly handed-over towers in a multi-phase Bangsar project, with private lobbies and eight units a floor. Sean likes the address and layouts, but questions a pool beside an affordable housing block and the messy access.
takeaways: A 917 sq ft two-bedroom lists at about RM970,000, near RM1,000 psf, and rents for about RM4,500 to RM4,600 furnished.
Each floor has eight units around a core of five passenger lifts, with no fire doors to pass through.
Only two towers are handed over so far, so access is cramped and the site still messy.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Bangsar Hill Park is a multi-phase development whose towers D and E have been handed over first. They share a drop-off and central lobby, then each has a private, card-controlled lobby. Each floor has eight units in four wings around a core with five passenger lifts and voids that bring daylight to the lift lobby. Facilities include a rooftop viewing deck with whirlpools, a multi-tier pool, an indoor playground, a large Life Fitness gym with saunas and a dance studio, and a water garden.

Sean viewed a 917 sq ft two-bedroom, two-bathroom unit with a ceiling of about 3 m, a U-shaped kitchen with an Elba oven and Electrolux hob, engineered hardwood in the bedrooms, a long balcony and a master bathroom with a Kohler bathtub.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project sits on Lorong Maarof, parallel to Jalan Maarof among landed homes, with views over Bukit Gasing, KL Eco City, Mid Valley and the KL skyline. Bangsar South, KL Sentral, Damansara Heights, PJ, Publika and Mont Kiara are close, the LRT is a 10 to 15-minute walk, and shops, Telawi and Bangsar Shopping Centre are nearby. An affordable housing block stands right beside the pool deck.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Listings ask about RM970,000 for this unit type from the developer, close to RM1,000 psf, and fully furnished two-bedroom units rent for about RM4,500 to RM4,600 a month.

standout.title: Eight units, no fire doors
standout.body: The lift core sits in the middle of the floor with eight units arranged in four wings around it, and voids let daylight into the lobby. Coming home feels open rather than like walking down a corridor, every unit gets plenty of facade, and some gain an extra window onto the void.

pros: The location: Maarof's connections to Bangsar South, KL Eco City, KL Sentral, PJ, Publika, Mont Kiara and Damansara Heights, with shops on the same road and public transport within reach.

The design: a shared drop-off leading to private lobbies with an extra card check, well-dressed common areas, eight units a floor in four open wings, and luxurious two-bedroom units with a bathtub and an extra window by the void.
The facilities and the handling of a complicated phased handover, with the garden area his favourite and the car park well partitioned between phases.
cons: It is messy: a narrow entrance, double and triple parking, jams at the security point and spillover parking among the neighbouring landed homes, so first impressions aren't grand yet.
The pool and spa pool sit right beside an existing affordable housing block; he would have swapped them with the more private garden area.
Many new projects are coming up nearby, such as The Lantern and Federal Hill, raising competition and density, though eight units a floor keeps it feeling exclusive.

closing: A well-designed home with a prestigious Bangsar address and strong rents, once the rest of the development is complete.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this December 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view her unit after handover; prices and rents are from listings as he quoted them.
